calls.title: Growthbook <> Opendoor - Check In
calls.summary: The meeting outlined progress on the proof of concept for Growth Book, highlighting the successful completion of security approval and Okta integration, which enabled activation of the Enterprise trial. The trial, now extended to 30 days, allows for uninterrupted testing. The data integration strategy involves connecting a Snowflake data pipeline and initiating an AA test to validate data flows. A product demo is scheduled for July 9th to demonstrate key features, with documentation shared beforehand. A multi-timezone support team has been established for technical assistance, and pricing discussions are set to align with existing provider benchmarks. Effective scheduling practices were discussed to maximize client participation.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Opendoor - Demo refresh
calls.summary: The meeting addressed the progress of GrowthBook's proof of concept, highlighting the successful launch of an initial AA test with data integration and a planned B test on the homepage hero section. The discussion included features like flexible targeting, segmentation, and robust experiment management capabilities. Metrics cataloging and detailed statistical analyses were emphasized, demonstrating GrowthBook's analytical power. Challenges related to user identity mapping and the necessity for cleanup of legacy IDs were acknowledged, as were plans for upcoming features such as funnel analysis and user journey mapping. Support mechanisms, including 24/7 assistance and automated monitoring, were also outlined to ensure seamless operational readiness.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Opendoor - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: The discussion centered on aligning Growth Book’s pricing proposal with Opendoor's spending patterns, proposing a $100,000 platform fee plus seat fees to match their $200,000 budget for 150 seats. Dan Wathne emphasized the proposal's flexibility, allowing for discounts and potential phased access based on actual usage. Contract signing is targeted for July, with coordination for procurement led by Siva. Growth Book commits to 24/7 support and rapid feature requests, ensuring a user-friendly experience. Both teams expressed a desire for a long-term partnership, focusing on sustainable collaboration, while Growth Book's open-source nature was highlighted as a competitive advantage amid concerns around rival companies.

calls.title: Opendoor<>GrowthBook - Discussion
calls.summary: The meeting addressed urgent contract negotiations between OpenDoor and Growthbook, emphasizing a need to finalize terms and pricing amidst limited legal resources. Abbie Thomsen highlighted the critical end-of-month deadline, and Jake Heier discussed potential pricing flexibility due to budget constraints. The team sought to reduce the contract from $210K to $170K, with a possible 10% discount through marketing collaboration that would enhance OpenDoor's profile. Legal and procurement processes were actively moving forward, with a single lawyer at OpenDoor prioritizing contract review. Both parties showed commitment to open communication and a strong partnership, highlighting operational readiness following a successful POC phase.
calls.keywords: Pricing negotiation, contract addendum, legal review, InfoSec security, procurement process, marketing collaboration
